value.body: An architect designs buildings and spaces, prepares drawings and coordinates with clients, engineers and contractors through construction. Architecture firms, real-estate developers, government public works departments and design consultancies hire architects, and many later set up their own practice. A typical day is design work, drawing revisions, client meetings and site visits.

items.label: Registration
items.note: Required to use the title "architect" under the Architects Act, 1972

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Admission to B.Arch is through NATA or JEE Main Paper 2. After graduating, freshers register with the Council of Architecture and usually join a firm as a junior architect. A portfolio of design studio work matters in hiring.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Coordinating with consultants and site teams

value.title: At a glance
items: Early-career pay is often modest; experience and a portfolio drive progression.
Typical path: junior architect, project architect, then associate or own practice.
An M.Arch or M.Plan is an option for specialisation or teaching.

competition.note: B.Arch graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
